# Renderer notes, program render round 1 (renderer agent a71fb064e2c143e4e; saved verbatim by the coordinator). Render published (55 docs, DOCS OK); the renderer judged none of these a rule-vs-compute mismatch.
1. Zero termination fee: the termination-notice tool always books a fee line, even at 0.00. That conflicts with the base rule that a zero line is not billed. It only matters on Starter/Growth tiers (0 fee months) or when no 30-day period is left.
2. No platform-fee line: Starter/Growth have a 0.00 platform fee, so no platform-fee line exists. The SLA credit base and the claim tool's line reference assume one, and the rule does not say what happens without it.
3. Whole-month windows: the look-back windows ("fewer than N whole months … to today") do not state how whole months are counted. I used the day-of-month convention the same rules state for other counts, which matches the compute. It makes a difference only at month ends.
4. Two bindings sit in the calculation document's coverage but are defined in a factor document's prose: the returned amount (return late charge) and the first day of the claim month (SLA credit). Each is used by only one factor, but the source lists neither among that factor's bindings. This is a placement point only.
